subject: project:gdl
value: A ZERO-VALUED TRAILING CLAIM SLACK PAYS ONLY WHEN A DECLARED SYMBOL OWNS THE PAD; WHEN THE PAD IS UNOWNED, SHRINKING THE CLAIM IS A STRICT REGRESSION. claim.law.splits-claim-can-swallow-link-alignment-padding tells you to shrink such a claim, and its three tells (datadiff 'claim slack(zero)', a neighbouring odd-address claim end, a symbols.txt size/type inconsistency) are all real — but tell (1) fires in BOTH the paying and the non-paying case, so following the prescription on tell (1) alone loses matched_data. THE DECISIVE TEST, one grep of symbols.txt: find the LAST declared symbol inside the claim and add its size to its address. (a) If that end lands SHORT of the claim end, the slack bytes are UNOWNED, dtk covers them with a .hidden gap symbol, objdiff already EXCLUDES that symbol so the section is ALREADY scoring 100% and already earning its matched_data — shrinking removes real bytes from both numerator and denominator and strictly loses. This is the general form of the sysservice special case. (b) If the last symbol's declared size OVERRUNS the object's true end, that symbol OWNS the pad, no gap symbol is created, objdiff compares a longer target section against our shorter one, the section scores below 100% and earns ZERO matched_data — shrinking BOTH the splits end and that symbol's size recovers the section's full credit. Case (b) always announces itself as tell (3), a symbol whose declared size contradicts its data type (fakelib's lbl_80348A70 was size:0x8 align:4 data:float — a float is 4 bytes, and align:4 confirms the float, while consistent siblings read size:0x4 float or size:0x8 align:8 double). So TELL (3) IS THE DECISIVE ONE AND TELL (1) IS MERELY NECESSARY. CORRECTION TO THE PARENT LAW'S STATED DISCRIMINATOR: the parent law and the objdiff-gap law together imply 4-byte alignment of the true end is what separates the shrinkable from the non-shrinkable (mb_font worked because its ends were 4-aligned; sysservice's 0x801177B5 was not). That is NOT the operative variable — it only governs whether dtk ACCEPTS the edit. Measured directly: cardutil's true end 0x801176AE is NOT 4-aligned and dtk accepted the shrink with no alignment error at all, yet it still lost 2 bytes, because the pad was unowned. Alignment governs legality; SYMBOL OWNERSHIP governs whether it pays. IMAGE-WIDE CENSUS (all 57 NonMatching units, datadiff plain + --sections, 2026-09-01): exactly four claim-slack sites exist. fakelib .sdata2 0x4 zero = case (b), FIXED this pass. cardutil .rodata 0x2 zero = case (a), measured regression, DO NOT SHRINK. auxanim .rodata 0x2 zero = case (a) by the same arithmetic (last symbol lbl_801116C4 size:0x26 ends at 0x801116EA, exactly our object size), DO NOT SHRINK — disposed of without spending a build. action .data 0x8 slack is NONZERO and therefore neither case: nonzero trailing bytes mean genuinely missing data, not padding, and the shrink prescription must not be applied to it at all. The data-gate half of the flip frontier is therefore now fully enumerated and closed: no further matched_data is available from claim-slack work anywhere in the image.
